- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimate later — adjust downward gradually after initial spike.
- Overshoot after sharp upward spikes (e.g., 79.23 → 81.98) — cap forecast at +10% above recent peak or use moving average smoothing.
- Underestimate when true values are trending upward — increase forecast by 1–2% of recent 7-day average if price > 80.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >85% of 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- Lagged bias: if true value is higher than forecast by >2% for 3 consecutive days, adjust next forecast down by 0.5–1.5%.
- Avoid overfitting to recent highs — if last 5 days are above 80, don’t forecast >82 unless confirmed by 2+ consecutive days.
